topic: Why an agreement is not always a contract
headline_fact: An agreement must meet legal conditions before it becomes an enforceable contract.
summary: An agreement and an enforceable contract are different ideas. This lesson introduces the distinction through a familiar purchase.
did_you_know: Some transactions also need writing, witnesses or registration.
core_mechanics: The law considers the agreement, the parties, consent, consideration, purpose and other applicable requirements.
why_it_matters: Recognizing the conditions helps explain why agreement alone does not settle enforceability.

in_depth_breakdown.real_world_application: Consider the full context before assuming a promise is enforceable.

indian_law_lesson.question: Does every agreement become an enforceable contract?
indian_law_lesson.learning_goal: Understand why an agreement needs legal conditions before a court can enforce it.

opening_scenario.title: An everyday purchase
opening_scenario.situation: Imagine two adults agree on a price for a used bicycle. One promises to pay, and the other promises to deliver it.
opening_scenario.question: Is agreement alone enough to settle every legal question?

plain_rule.explanation: A contract is an agreement that the law can enforce. An agreement alone does not establish every condition. The parties, their consent, what they exchange and the purpose also matter.

legal_basis.title: Agreement and enforceability
legal_basis.plain_meaning: The Act distinguishes agreements from enforceable contracts and sets conditions for enforceability.
legal_basis.legal_effect: An agreement must satisfy the applicable legal conditions. Other laws can also require particular formalities.

applicability.jurisdiction: An introductory explanation of the Indian Contract Act. Particular transactions can involve other applicable laws.
who_it_concerns: People entering agreements that may have legal effect.
applicability.relevant_dates: The Act dates from 1872. This lesson does not independently check later changes or the law applicable to a particular transaction.
conditions: The parties must have legal capacity to contract.
The exchange and purpose must meet legal requirements.
The agreement must not be expressly declared void.
exceptions: Some transactions also require writing, witnesses or registration under other laws.
limits: This is an introduction, not a decision about a real dispute.
The actual facts and applicable law can change the analysis.

key_terms.definition: A legal obligation that a court can require a party to meet.
Something exchanged for a promise, as understood under the Act.

explanation_steps.title: Identify what the parties agreed
explanation_steps.explanation: Start with the promises. The example involves a bicycle and an agreed payment.

explanation_steps.title: Check the legal conditions
explanation_steps.explanation: Ask whether the parties can contract and whether consent, the exchange and the purpose satisfy the law.

explanation_steps.title: Check other requirements
explanation_steps.explanation: Do not assume that an agreement alone satisfies every law. The type of transaction may introduce further requirements.

worked_example.title: Look beyond the agreed price
worked_example.situation: In the hypothetical bicycle purchase, both parties are adults. The example gives only a few facts.
reasoning_steps: Consider the exchange, purpose and other legal requirements.
worked_example.implications: The agreed price is part of the analysis. It does not answer every legal question.
worked_example.limits: The example does not establish the outcome of a real dispute.

contrast_example.title: Change the transaction
contrast_example.situation: Now imagine an agreement about property that may require registration.
reasoning_steps: Identify the different kind of transaction.
Check the additional law and its formal requirements.
contrast_example.implications: The required formalities may change even though both parties agree.
contrast_example.limits: The property and transaction details determine which requirements apply.

common_confusions.confusion: Both people agreed, so the law must enforce it.
common_confusions.clarification: Agreement is the starting point. The law also sets conditions and may impose further requirements.

knowledge_checks.question: Does an agreed price prove every condition for a contract?
knowledge_checks.explanation: It does not establish capacity, free consent or every other applicable condition.

takeaways: An agreement and an enforceable contract are different ideas.
Check the legal conditions, not just the promises.
